sentence: Every frown begins at the end of a nerve.
claim: A facial muscle is told to contract by the motor nerve ending that supplies it, at the neuromuscular junction.
source_title: Physiology, Neuromuscular Junction (StatPearls; editor P. C. Bollu, updated 17 Feb 2025)
note: [OPEN] Not on a page I could read (StatPearls 403; Bookshelf reCAPTCHA). PMC2856357 only implies it ('inhibiting the release of acetylcholine from presynaptic motor neurons'). A person opens a neuromuscular-junction source. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: The nerve lets out a chemical messenger called acetylcholine.
claim: The motor nerve ending releases acetylcholine, the main chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) at the neuromuscular junction.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Read 8 Nov: 'blocking the release of acetylcholine, which is the principal neurotransmitter at the neuromuscular junction'; '…from presynaptic motor neurons'. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: It reaches a muscle fibre, which gets the message and pulls.
claim: Released acetylcholine makes the muscle fibre contract.
source_title: Physiology, Neuromuscular Junction (StatPearls; editor P. C. Bollu, updated 17 Feb 2025)
note: [OPEN] Implied only (PMC2856357: blocking ACh release causes muscle paralysis). Needs a neuromuscular-junction page a person opens. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: Botulinum toxin gets inside that nerve ending.
claim: Botulinum toxin is taken up into the motor nerve ending, where its light chain acts.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Read 8 Nov: bound 'to high affinity receptors at the presynaptic surface of cholinergic neurones, and the toxin-receptor complex is taken up into the cell by endocytosis… the toxin escapes into the cytoplasm'. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: There it cuts one protein, SNAP-25, that the message needs.
claim: Type A's light chain is a protease that cleaves SNAP-25, a protein needed for acetylcholine vesicles to fuse with the membrane (other serotypes cut VAMP or syntaxin).
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [OPEN] PMC2856357 (read) says the light chain 'interact[s] with … SNAP 25, vesicle associated membrane protein and syntaxin … to prevent fusion of acetylcholine vesicles'; it does not say 'cleaves'. The coordinator states type A cleaves SNAP-25 specifically (VAMP/syntaxin are other serotypes' targets). Needs a page that says 'cleaves' (nature.com and PubMed were blocked when tried): OPEN. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: The message stays stuck, so the muscle gets no signal and the frown can relax.
claim: With acetylcholine release blocked the muscle is weakened; frown lines are made by the pull of the glabellar muscles.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] PMC2856357: 'causing muscle paralysis' by 'inhibiting the release of acetylcholine'. Frown lines: PMC9032255 (Toxins 2022): 'Glabellar frown lines are created by three muscles: the corrugator supercilii… procerus and depressor supercilii'. 'Can relax' is hedged: effect varies by person and muscle; a dermatologist confirms. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: Two hundred years ago, a German doctor named Justinus Kerner studied a poison in spoiled sausages that caused paralysis.
claim: In 1817–1822 Kerner gave the first accurate descriptions of food-borne botulism ('sausage poisoning').
source_title: From poison to remedy: the chequered history of botulinum toxin (Erbguth FJ; J Neural Transm, 2008)
note: [OPEN] Carried over from the earlier draft (PubMed excerpt: Kerner's 1820 monograph on 'sausage poisoning' reviewed 76 cases). PubMed page not readable here; OPEN. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: He guessed it might one day become a medicine.
claim: Kerner proposed a possible therapeutic use of the toxin; he speculated, he did not test it.
source_title: From poison to remedy: the chequered history of botulinum toxin (Erbguth FJ; J Neural Transm, 2008)
note: [OPEN] Carried over: Kerner 'also suggested a possible therapeutic use'. OPEN. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

claim: The weakness from type A usually wears off over about three months.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Read 8 Nov: 'The weakness induced by injection with botulinum toxin A usually lasts about three months.' Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: The nerve slowly grows new endings, and about three months later the message flows again.
claim: Function recovers by sprouting of nerve terminals and new synaptic contacts, usually in two to three months.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Read 8 Nov: 'The affected nerve terminals do not degenerate, but the blockage of neurotransmitter release is irreversible. Function can be recovered by the sprouting of nerve terminals and formation of new synaptic contacts; this usually takes two to three months.' (mostly animal work: badge says so). Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: So a frown is a message, and this toxin blocks it.
claim: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Read 8 Nov: 'acts at the neuromuscular junction to cause muscle paralysis by inhibiting the release of acetylcholine from presynaptic motor neurons'. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.

sentence: The skin was never the target.
claim: The toxin's effect is at the nerve-muscle junction, not on the skin itself.
source_title: Botulinum toxin (Nigam PK, Nigam A; Indian Journal of Dermatology, 2010)
note: [SOURCE-READ] Same quote as s11. The page never says 'not the skin': the film's plain-words reading; dermatologist to confirm. Treatment topic: dermatologist sign-off.
